lines.trans: You messed with the man, you messed with the man.
There is no kid here.
Tell him, my moderator, there is no kid here.
It is a lot, it is a lot of strength.
What is going on?
Take that, take this right here, look.
Feel the angel. Feel the angel.
Look at the water maker.

meanings.note: With com, mexer com alguém means to mess with or provoke someone.
Marks accompaniment or an added ingredient such as sweetener.

examples.text: Ela está com a nossa equipe.

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Adult male human; plural homens.
A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.
Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: Colloquial Brazilian word for boy or inexperienced kid.
Irregular 3rd singular present diz.
Links verbs like faltar to an event or destination.
Third-person masculine singular subject pronoun.
First-person singular possessive agreeing with the thing possessed.

examples.text: O seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?

meanings.note: Person moderating a debate or discussion.
Used for identifying a type of meeting or the department a person belongs to. The present forms sou and é are irregular.
Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Very frequent general noun; singular muita coisa naturally translates as a lot of things.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

examples.text: Deixa eu te falar uma coisa.

meanings.note: Physical or moral strength; also used as encouragement (Força!).

examples.text: É muita coisa, é muita força.
examples.trans: It is a lot, it is a lot of strength.
He has a lot of strength.

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Used in O que está acontecendo? (What is going on?) and O que aconteceu foi que... (What happened was that...).
Standard verb for having coffee, tea, water, or soup.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?
I have coffee in the morning.

meanings.note: Points to the speaker's location or reinforces demonstratives like isso aqui and esse slide aqui.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.

meanings.note: Spoken clipping of olha! used at the end of a phrase to draw visual attention.

examples.trans: Take that, take this right here, look.

meanings.note: Informal imperative sente (feel!).
Literally angel; also used affectionately or playfully in Brazilian Portuguese.
Used as a quick imperative olha! (look!) and in future subjunctive se vocês olharem (if you look).

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: Agent noun from formar (to form or shape).

examples.text: Ele é um formador de opinião.

meanings.note: Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Everyday noun for water.

examples.trans: I want a glass of water.

meanings.note: In até logo it looks ahead to the next meeting. The phrase is added as the lesson farewell, not quoted from the selected source window.
Marks comparisons (mais que), negated continuation (não ... mais, not anymore), and the farewell até mais.
